# pooltime

> pooltime pools several Claude Max/Pro and ChatGPT (Codex) subscription accounts behind one local
> Anthropic-compatible endpoint (http://127.0.0.1:3460) for Claude Code. macOS and Linux. One binary,
> data in ~/.pooltime. This file is for coding agents setting pooltime up for a user: every step
> below is non-interactive unless it says a human must act.

Rules for agents:
- Never print, log or paste tokens, ~/.pooltime/run/*.key, or credentials files.
- Signing in needs the human: they open a URL in a browser and sign in. Do not try to automate it.
- Only connect the Claude Code profiles the user names. Do not use `pooltime connect --all` unless
  they ask for every ~/.claude* profile.
- If bro-cli is in use, the user must stop it (`bro pool down`) before pooltime serves imported accounts.
- These steps need pooltime v1.0.0 or later (main branch). `pooltime --version` shows the version.

## 1. Install

```sh
brew install chrisjenx/tap/pooltime
```

or, without Homebrew (installs to ~/.local/bin, no sudo; make sure it is on PATH):

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrisjenx/pooltime/main/install.sh | sh
```

Check:

```sh run
pooltime --version
```

## 2. Non-interactive setup

`pooltime setup` with `--yes` never asks; it does only what the flags say. Flags:

- `--import-bro`: import accounts/settings from bro-cli (when ~/.claude-max-pool or ~/.bro exists and
  pooltime has no accounts yet).
- `--account NAME`: sign in a first Claude account (when pooltime has none and nothing is imported).
  Needs the human (see step 3). Optional `--email EMAIL`, `--mode callback|paste`.
- `--service`: install the background service (launchd on macOS, systemd --user on Linux).
- `--connect PROFILES`: comma-separated Claude Code profile ids to connect: `default` = ~/.claude,
  `claude-personal` = ~/.claude-personal, etc.
- `--yes` / `-y`: never ask; also binds a first sign-in to the account without asking.

Migrating from bro (ask the user to run `bro pool down` first):

```sh
pooltime setup --import-bro --service --connect default --yes
```

Fresh install, first Claude account signed in by the human, then service and one profile:

```sh
pooltime setup --account personal --email you@example.com --service --connect default --yes
```

setup prints one line per step, runs `pooltime doctor`, then prints the dashboard URL. Exit 1 if a
step or a doctor check failed. It is safe to re-run.

Then add the status line segment and the MCP server to the connected profiles (setup does not do
this yet):

```sh
pooltime connect default --statusline --mcp
```

## 3. Sign-in (the human must act)

Claude account:

```sh
pooltime accounts login personal
```

With a local browser this opens it and waits up to 5 minutes for the redirect.

Headless / SSH (pooltime picks paste mode automatically when `SSH_TTY` is set, or on Linux without
DISPLAY/WAYLAND_DISPLAY; force it with `--mode paste`): pooltime prints a URL. The human opens it in
any browser, signs in, and pastes the `code#state` line the page shows at the `Code:` prompt on
stdin. Run the command where the human can type into it.

```sh
pooltime accounts login personal --mode paste
```

ChatGPT / Codex account:

```sh
pooltime accounts add codex-1 --provider openai --login
```

The browser is redirected to http://localhost:1455/auth/callback (or 1457). Headless options:
1. On the human's laptop, forward the ports, then open the printed URL there; it finishes by itself:
   `ssh -L 1455:127.0.0.1:1455 -L 1457:127.0.0.1:1457 user@server`
2. Or, after signing in, the browser lands on a page that fails to load: paste that full address
   at the `Code:` prompt.

Reuse an existing Codex CLI sign-in instead (no browser; pooltime then owns it, so the Codex CLI
needs `codex login` again):

```sh
pooltime accounts add codex-1 --provider openai --from-codex-auth
```

Re-login later: `pooltime accounts relogin --dead` or `--expiring` (one at a time, same modes).

## 4. Linux service persistence

A systemd user service stops when the user logs out. On servers / SSH-only machines:

```sh
loginctl enable-linger "$USER"
pooltime service install
pooltime service status
```

## 5. Verify

```sh
pooltime doctor
pooltime status
pooltime accounts list
```

`doctor` exits 1 on any failure and prints the command that fixes each problem. Each account shows
one state: ready, expiring, rate_limited, erroring, access_denied, billing, needs_login.

## 6. Use

Start `claude` in a connected profile; nothing else to configure. `pooltime open` prints and opens
the dashboard URL (it contains a local key: do not share it). `pooltime disconnect` restores the
profiles' own settings; `pooltime service uninstall` disconnects every profile and removes the service.

## Commands

```sh run
pooltime --help
pooltime setup --help
pooltime accounts --help
```
